reports.desc: Received a package that was not ordered, not once, but twice. Two different addresses, but the same company. Very confused on how we received these packages, thankfully no money was lost, at least to our knowledge. Shipped to us VIA USPS ground advantage.

Mail sent to our office indicating our Domain name was expiring and a 5 year renewal was due and needed. Person paying did not know or realize they did not hold our domain. Attempts to immediately cancel the charge were made, but person's via the "support" email were rude and ignored requests for cancelation and refund.

Scammer sent an invoice appearing to be a renewal for the domain name. They were and are not the domain holders and the domain was not expired or expiring as they indicated.
Office person paid "bill" not realizing they were not the domain holder and no renewal was needed

Facebook popup. They offered stretch pants that were really nice. 6" Stretch at waist. Only offered 3XL and 4XL for larger sizes, I ordered size 3X which I always use. I received a size 16. This is nowhere near what is a size 3XL in other online offers. The reason I'm calling it a scam because of the address and no information inside of package for contacting the company.

The Royal Lion Glass Whiskey Decanter Set that I ordered from the photos posted on their website is not the same product depicted and delivered to me. Their photos show a larger, finely crafted decanter with an ornate crown, a solid blue treasure chest, and a glass lion with hollow legs capable of holding additional beverages. It also shows the decanter in a felt-lined decanter box. The item I received has a cheap plastic crown, a small glass box with a sticker-like decal, and solid glass legs and tail. It arrived in a cardboard box packed in Styrofoam, is about one-third the size pictured on the website, and is far less valuable than the $47 that I was charged.  The company offered a $10 refund or a $15 refund if I did not report it to the BBB.

Since October 2025, I have received over 600 unsolicited prerecorded calls promoting supposed personal loans/debt relief. I have NEVER applied for a loan, answered these calls, returned a call, or consented to these solicitations. The callers continually rotate/spoof caller-ID numbers while directing recipients to recurring callback numbers using fictitious stories. Recent messages claim I have an existing “file,” that supervisors/underwriters have reviewed it, and, often lately, that numerous employees have repeatedly tried to reach me. This caller identified themself as "Carla lending department" and offered an unsolicited $70,000 unsecured personal loan, saying it bet lunch with the entire floor that she would get me on the phone today. Other recordings use similar fictitious personal stories and loan approvals. I have preserved numerous voicemails, screenshots, dates, caller-ID numbers and callback numbers and have reported this lawbreaker to the FTC numerous times.
Tried keeping in touch by email they would say on the way

company advertised extra large boxes from returned pallets. special if you buy 2. See product description.jpg.  Then they add shipping and "tip."  What I received was a phone charging cable and a base in a padded envelope. Also shown in attachment. They refuse to provide refund or acknowledge the scam, deceitfulness, and completely inappropriate marketing scheme to dupe people out of money.

I placed an order. I checked for delivery, and I was told oops, we're running late granted. This was over 3 months ago, at least\n And I was told, oh, we'll just have to pay shipping again and you can get your product. But they didn't, and it's been a scam, I've been contacting for months.
I received a phone call from (unavailable) asking me to press any number then the pound key, when I did that it disconnected. My credit card has been compromised and I believe this may be part of it.
